rows.title: Performance degradation with webjars locator
rows.excerpt:
Hello, 
we see a significant regression on performance on some of Arm servers which is introduced by this patch (I didn't test on x86): 

```
commit 91f55a4f7134409a832435de2c6df231102d5898 (HEAD -> head-2)
Author: Dave Syer <dsyer@vmware.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 27 08:32:30 2024 +0000
 
    Versionless webjars (again)
 
    Spring Boot 3.4 supports the webjars-locator-lite which in turn
    supports native images, so we are back to versionless URLs for
    webjars assets in templates.
```
    
The performance drop introduced is quite severe, going from 3.3k req/s on this little test to about 0.7k req/s. 
   
```
user@PetClinic-test:~$ numactl -C 16 wrk -c 1 -t 1 http://localhost:8080 -d 60
Running 1m test @ http://localhost:8080
  1 threads and 1 connections
  Thread Stats   Avg      Stdev     Max   +/- Stdev
    Latency     1.36ms   15.88ms 359.72ms   99.44%
    Req/Sec     3.37k   453.34     3.79k    93.80%
  200156 requests in 1.00m, 579.75MB read
**Requests/sec:   3335.91**
Transfer/sec:      9.66MB

Running 1m test @ http://localhost:8080

**Requests/sec:    694.05**
Transfer/sec:      2.01MB
user@PetClinic-test:~$
```

These are the steps to repro on Ubuntu. 
Server: 
```
    sudo apt update
    sudo apt install numactl wrk maven openjdk-17-jdk
    git clone https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-petclinic.git
    cd spring-petclinic/
    ./mvnw package
    numactl -C 0-7 java -jar target/*.jar

```
Client: 
`    numactl -C 16 wrk -c 1 -t 1 http://localhost:8080 -d 60
`

rows.excerpt:
# CloudSmith Troubleshooting Summary
## Trigger details
| Workflow run  | Branch  | Commit  |
|---|---|---|
| [#15837158459](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-petclinic/actions/runs/15837158459) |  ```facError``` |  ```25cf7e2c3fc337b119c09b5a102f0e5b6c829e6c``` |
----
## Detailed Findings
### Issue 1


**Problem**: The application fails to start because port 8080 is already in use. This is a port conflict issue where another process is already using the default port configured in application.properties.


**File**: ```src/main/resources/application.properties```


**Error Log**:
```
2025-06-23T23:16:02.8607484Z out: Description:\n2025-06-23T23:16:02.8608003Z out: Web server failed to start. Port 8080 was already in use.\n2025-06-23T23:16:02.8608706Z out: Action:\n2025-06-23T23:16:02.8608706Z out: Identify and stop the process that\'s listening on port 8080 or configure this application to listen on another port.
```


**Code snippet**:
```
server.address=0.0.0.0\nserver.port=8080\n# Prefer IPv4 stack\nserver.tomcat.protocol-header-https-value=java.net.preferIPv4Stack=true
```


**Solution Plan**:


1. Modify the application.properties file to use a different port: Using port 0 will make Spring Boot automatically select an available port.
```
                   server.address=0.0.0.0
                   server.port=0
                   # Prefer IPv4 stack
                   server.tomcat.protocol-header-https-value=java.net.preferIPv4Stack=true
```
2. Alternatively, you can specify a specific unused port like 8081:
```
                   server.port=8081
```
3. For the CI/CD environment, you can also add a step to kill any process using port 8080 before starting the application:
```
                   lsof -ti:8080 | xargs kill -9 || true
```

## Summary

This PR improves documentation for selected service-layer/business-logic classes in the current Spring PetClinic project.

## Changes Made

- Added class-level Javadoc to `OwnerController`, `PetController`, and `VetController`.
- Added Javadoc to public constructors.
- Added Javadoc to public controller methods.
- Documented method responsibilities, parameters, return values, and applicable exceptions.
- Improved clarity around owner, pet, and veterinarian workflows.
- Preserved existing application logic without changing functionality.

## Files Updated

- `OwnerController.java`
- `PetController.java`
- `VetController.java`

## Rationale

These documentation updates make the code easier for new contributors to understand and maintain. Clear Javadoc reduces onboarding time, lowers reliance on informal knowledge from existing developers, and helps prevent knowledge silos. It also supports technical sustainability by making controller responsibilities and expected behaviours easier to identify before future changes are made.

## Testing

- Documentation-only change.
- No functional behaviour was changed.
- Existing code structure and logic were preserved.

rows.title: Refactor: remove unnecessary imports and redundant intermediate variables
rows.excerpt:
## Summary
This PR removes unnecessary imports and eliminates redundant intermediate variables across three controllers and two test files, as part of the sustainable coding practices evaluation for SE754 Assignment 5.

## Problem
Manual inspection and SonarQube analysis identified two categories of redundant code across the `owner` package.

**Unnecessary imports** - `OwnerControllerTests.java` and `VetControllerTests.java` both had a class-level import for `MockMvcRequestBuilders` despite already having static imports for the individual methods (`get`, `post`) from the same class. This made the class-level import redundant and unused. Similarly, `OwnerController.java`, `PetController.java`, and `VisitController.java` each imported `java.util.Optional` which was only needed to hold an intermediate variable that was immediately unwrapped on the next line.

**Redundant intermediate variables** - In `OwnerController.java`, `PetController.java`, and `VisitController.java`, the pattern of assigning `owners.findById(...)` to an `optionalOwner` variable and then calling `.orElseThrow(...)` on the very next line served no purpose. SonarQube flags this under `java:S1488` - local variables should not be declared and then immediately returned or used.

## Changes
- Replaced `MockMvcRequestBuilders.post(...)` and `MockMvcRequestBuilders.get(...)` with the already-imported static equivalents in `OwnerControllerTests.java` and `VetControllerTests.java`, and removed the now-unused class-level imports
- Collapsed all `optionalOwner` intermediate variable declarations into single chained expressions using `.orElseThrow(...)` directly on the repository call in `OwnerController.java`, `PetController.java`, and `VisitController.java`
- Removed the `java.util.Optional` import from each controller where it was no longer referenced

## Sustainability Impact
Redundant code and unnecessary imports increase the noise developers must read through when understanding or modifying a file. Unused imports can mislead future contributors into thinking a type is meaningfully used, and they accumulate silently over time if not caught early.

## Files Changed
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/OwnerController.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclin
